methodology.notes: Cortex 0.1 is a cognitive architecture from Principled Machines. A cognitive core directs the work; a language model is one kind of compute it uses, for semantic judgement, and other parts of a task go to retrieval, programs and other specialized components. We attribute the result to two mechanisms: enhanced retrieval for multi-hop questions over the knowledge base, and process-calculus abstractions for the policy workflows. Submitted as custom because Cortex replaces the standard single-model scaffold. No task-specific fine-tuning, no prompt tuning against the grader, no post-training on labels, and no autoresearch loop. Cost is the average agent spend per trajectory, excluding the user simulator. Write-up: https://principledmachines.com/research/tau3-banking/

verification.details: Verified by Sierra on 2026-11-03: all 97 banking_knowledge tasks, 1 trial, run independently with the submitter's cortex_tau2.py client in --local mode at commit b7ea9074. Only agent calls went to the Cortex endpoint (cortex-0.1, reasoning_effort medium); the user simulator (gpt-5.2, reasoning_effort low) and all grading ran on Sierra's side with Sierra's keys. 71/97 passed (pass^1 73.20%); no infrastructure errors. Published scores and trajectories are from this run. The submitter's own 4-trial run reported 78.35% pass^1; pass^2-4 are omitted because the verified run has 1 trial. Caveats: knowledge-base retrieval runs on the Cortex server and is not visible in the trajectories (the submitter states the index contains only the banking_knowledge documents), and the hosted endpoint is not a frozen snapshot, so the result reflects cortex-0.1 as served on 2026-11-03. Cost is the submitter's reported average agent spend.
